Stewart, Calculus: Early Transcendentals · Section 15.7 · Exercise 32

Six Iterated Integrals for a Tetrahedron

Problem

Express the integral

∭E​f(x,y,z)dV

as an iterated integral in six different ways. The solid E is bounded by the planes x=2, y=2, z=0, and x+y−2z=2.

Reading the solid

Each plane cuts a face of the solid. A corner is the common point of three of the planes:

x=2, z=0, x+y−2z=2 ⟹ y=0,
y=2, z=0, x+y−2z=2 ⟹ x=0,
x=2, y=2, z=0 ⟹ z=0,
x=2, y=2, x+y−2z=2 ⟹ z=1.

The corners are A=(2,0,0), B=(0,2,0), C=(2,2,0), and D=(2,2,1). The solid is the tetrahedron ABCD. Its faces are the triangle ABC in the plane z=0, the triangle ACD in the plane x=2, the triangle BCD in the plane y=2, and the triangle ABD in the plane x+y−2z=2.

Every point of the base has z=0 and x+y≥2, and the apex D gives x+y−2z=2. Thus E lies in the half-space x+y−2z≥2, together with x≤2, y≤2, and z≥0. Solve the first inequality for z:

z≤2x+y−2​.

The upper bound is negative when x+y<2, so the base is the triangle T={(x,y):0≤x≤2, 2−x≤y≤2}. The base has area 2 and the apex D has height 1, so the volume is 2/3.

Solution

Step 1 — Put z first

Fix a point (x,y) of the base T. The vertical fibre above it runs from the base to the sloping face:

0≤z≤2x+y−2​.

Integrate z first, then y, then x. The base T gives 0≤x≤2 and 2−x≤y≤2:

∭E​fdV=∫02​∫2−x2​∫0(x+y−2)/2​f(x,y,z)dzdydx.

Swap the two outer integrations. The same triangle T reads 0≤y≤2 and 2−y≤x≤2:

∭E​fdV=∫02​∫2−y2​∫0(x+y−2)/2​f(x,y,z)dzdxdy.

Step 2 — Put y first

Project E onto the xz-plane. The face x=2 and the face z=0 are vertical planes, and the sloping plane gives the lower limit for y:

x+y−2z≥2 ⟹ y≥2+2z−x.

The plane y=2 gives the upper limit. The projection is the triangle 0≤x≤2, 0≤z≤x/2, because the lower limit must not exceed 2:

∭E​fdV=∫02​∫0x/2​∫2+2z−x2​f(x,y,z)dydzdx.

Swap the two outer integrations again. The triangle 0≤x≤2, 0≤z≤x/2 also reads 0≤z≤1 and 2z≤x≤2:

∭E​fdV=∫01​∫2z2​∫2+2z−x2​f(x,y,z)dydxdz.

Step 3 — Put x first

The solid is symmetric in x and y: the planes x=2 and y=2 play the same role, and the sloping plane is symmetric under the exchange of x and y. Project E onto the yz-plane instead. The sloping plane gives the lower limit for x:

x≥2+2z−y,x≤2,

and the projection is the triangle 0≤y≤2, 0≤z≤y/2. Hence

∭E​fdV=∫02​∫0y/2​∫2+2z−y2​f(x,y,z)dxdzdy.

Swap the two outer integrations. The triangle 0≤y≤2, 0≤z≤y/2 also reads 0≤z≤1 and 2z≤y≤2:

∭E​fdV=∫01​∫2z2​∫2+2z−y2​f(x,y,z)dxdydz.

Step 4 — Check the six orders with f=1

Set f=1. Each iterated integral then returns the volume of E, which is 2/3. Substitute f=1 in the first order and integrate:

∫02​∫2−x2​2x+y−2​dydx=∫02​[4(x+y−2)2​]2−x2​dx=∫02​4x2​dx=32​.

The middle integral uses y=2, where the numerator is x, and y=2−x, where the numerator is 0. All six orders give 2/3 (see the verification section).

Answer

The six orders of integration are

​∫02​∫2−x2​∫0(x+y−2)/2​fdzdydx∫02​∫0x/2​∫2+2z−x2​fdydzdx∫02​∫0y/2​∫2+2z−y2​fdxdzdy​​∫02​∫2−y2​∫0(x+y−2)/2​fdzdxdy∫01​∫2z2​∫2+2z−x2​fdydxdz∫01​∫2z2​∫2+2z−y2​fdxdydz​

Every order equals the volume 2/3 when f=1.

Notation

SymbolMeaning
∭E​fdVThe triple integral of f over the solid E, the limit of sums of f times small volumes.
EThe tetrahedron with vertices A, B, C, D.
dVThe volume element, dV=dzdydx in any order of the three differentials.
A,B,C,DThe four vertices of E: (2,0,0), (0,2,0), (2,2,0), and (2,2,1).
x+y−2z=2The sloping face ABD. It meets the base along the line x+y=2.
TThe base triangle ABC in the plane z=0, 0≤x≤2, 2−x≤y≤2.
(x+y−2)/2The height of the sloping face above the point (x,y) of T.
2+2z−xThe value of y on the sloping face at fixed x and z, obtained from x+y−2z=2.

Verification

Three independent computations support the six orders.

  • part1_step1.py builds the tetrahedron from the four planes. The scalar triple product of the edges at A is −4, so the volume is 2/3=0.666666666667. The base has area 2 and the apex has height 1, which gives the same volume. A Monte Carlo estimate is 0.66758±0.00075, which is 1.23 standard errors above 2/3.
  • part1_step2.py evaluates all six orders with SymPy. With f=1 every order gives 2/3. With f=xyz every order gives 19/45, and the inner z-integral is xy(x+y−2)2/8.
  • part1_step3.py evaluates all six orders with 60-point Gauss-Legendre quadrature. With f=1 every order gives 0.666666666666669, with a spread of 8.882×10−16. With f=xyz the six orders give values from 0.422222222222220 to 0.422222222222228, a spread of 7.827×10−15. The exact value is 19/45=0.422222222222222. An mpmath computation of one order gives 0.6666666666666667.
